title: The Weil category
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, and the chosen algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0$ be a separated scheme of
finite type over $k_0$ in the conventions of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$.
For a finite intermediate extension $E/\Ql$ in $\Qlb$, use
$\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(X,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], namely the
raw rationalization of the integral category
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. These coefficient categories
are on the small pro-etale site, with completed integral coefficients;
no identification with a different coefficient model is made.

Write $\Phi_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$,
where $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$ on $k$, for the geometric-Frobenius
automorphism of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], with the geometric convention
of [def-tw-frobenius-action]. Write $P_E=\Phi_{X,E}^*$ for its pullback on
$\mathcal C_E$: the completed pullback of
[def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] at the integral stage followed by
rationalization, using the equivalence of small pro-etale sites induced
by the scheme automorphism
[lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Thus $\Phi_X^*K$ below
means this derived pullback. In this automorphism case, inverse image
is an exact equivalence with exact inverse. Applying the two inverse
functors to resolutions of strict towers identifies the derived inverse
limit of the transported reduction tower with transport of the original
derived inverse limit. Thus completed pullback here is coefficient
transport, and its inverse is the transport along $\Phi_X^{-1}$.

A *Weil complex* at $E$ on $X_0$ is a pair $(K,\varphi_K)$ with
$K\in\mathcal C_E$ and an isomorphism
$\varphi_K:P_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Define
$\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,E)$ to be the category of these fixed pairs
[def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Explicitly, a morphism
$(K,\varphi_K)\to(L,\varphi_L)$ is a morphism $u:K\to L$ in $\mathcal C_E$
satisfying
$$u\circ\varphi_K=\varphi_L\circ P_E(u).$$
Identities and composition are those of $\mathcal C_E$. The *strict*
version mentioned here uses these same pairs and all these commuting
morphisms; the definition supplies no alternative morphism groups and no
triangulated structure on the category of pairs.

For $E\subseteq F$ use the scalar-extension functor
$T_{F/E}:\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal C_F$, its normalized units and
associators, and the ambient pullback comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension],
restricted and rationalized for the automorphism $\Phi_X$. Here the
restriction uses the site equivalence above: it transports the completed
coefficient sheaf and reduction tower, compatible etale-origin witnesses,
and constructibility strata, with their bounds unchanged. This is the
isomorphism case of the comparison, whose constructible restriction is
conditional on preservation in the cited statement.
Write the comparison in the direction
$c_{F/E}:P_FT_{F/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{F/E}P_E$.
Define the transition functor on Weil complexes by
$$(K,\varphi_K)\longmapsto
(T_{F/E}K,\ T_{F/E}(\varphi_K)\circ c_{F/E,K}),
\qquad u\longmapsto T_{F/E}(u).$$

The $\Qlb$-version $\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,\Qlb)$ is the filtered
$2$-colimit of these finite-stage Weil categories, with the common-stage
convention of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. More explicitly, its objects
are pairs $(E,W)$ with $E$ in the directed set of finite intermediate
extensions [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set] and
$W\in\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,E)$. A morphism $(E,W)\to(F,V)$ is a class
$[M,u]$, where $M\supseteq E,F$ is a finite intermediate extension and
$u:T_{M/E}W\to T_{M/F}V$ is a commuting Weil morphism at $M$.
Write $a_{N,M,E,W}:T_{N/M}T_{M/E}W\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{N/E}W$
for the induced associator on Weil pairs. For $N\supseteq M$ define
$$u_N=a_{N,M,F,V}\circ T_{N/M}(u)\circ a_{N,M,E,W}^{-1}.$$
Representatives $[M,u]$ and $[M',u']$ agree if $u_N=u'_N$ for some
finite $N\supseteq M,M'$. Equivalently their Hom group is
$$\varinjlim_{M\supseteq E,F}
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,M)}(T_{M/E}W,T_{M/F}V)$$
[def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. The identity is represented by
$(E,\operatorname{id}_W)$. For $[M,u]:(E,W)\to(F,V)$ and
$[M',v]:(F,V)\to(G,Z)$, choose $N\supseteq M,M'$ and define their
composite to be $[N,v_N\circ u_N]$. Here "finite
subfield" always means finite over $\Ql$, not a field with finitely many
elements. This is a colimit of Weil categories, not a claim that the
underlying coefficient category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] already
includes Frobenius data.

Completed pullback is still the strict reduction-tower derived-limit construction; no arbitrary pullback preservation is used. The delivery tool rebases onto current origin during the required dry run. blueprint_update.statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite and let $X_0$ be a
separated scheme of finite type
over $\mathbf F_q$, with $X=X_0\otimes_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$.
A *Weil complex* $(K,\varphi_K)$ consists of
$K\in D^b_c(X,E)$ (the categories of
[def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]) and an isomorphism
$\varphi_K:\Phi_X^*K\cong K$, where $\Phi_X$ is the geometric
Frobenius of [def-tw-frobenius-action]; morphisms are morphisms
of $K$ commuting with the $\varphi$'s. The *Weil category*
$\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,E)$ has as objects the Weil complexes; its strict
version uses the same objects and all commuting morphisms. The
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-version is the filtered colimit over the
finite subfields $E$ of its finite-stage analogue (the
$2$-colimit of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]).
